Get the unit and measurement properties of a table's contents

Source: R/contents.R
get_contents.Rd

Returns one row per value of the table's contents variable (the measures), with the unit the source states for it. The unit is the fact a number cannot be read without (tkr or mnkr?), and it is not part of what get_variables() returns.

Usage

get_contents(api, table_id, verbose = FALSE)

Arguments

api

A <px_api> object.

table_id

A single table ID (character).

verbose

Print request details.

Value

A tibble with columns table_id, variable (the code of the contents variable), code, text, unit, decimals, measuring_type, price_type, adjustment, refperiod and base_period; or NULL when the API could not be reached.

Details

For a v2 API the table metadata carries the unit, together with the measuring type (stock or flow), price type (current or fixed), seasonal adjustment and reference period where the source states them. One request.

A v1 API states no unit in its table metadata, but answers a data request in json-stat2 form with the same block. get_contents() therefore asks for a single cell in that form, and once more for every value of the contents variable when there are several: at most two small data requests on top of the metadata. A v1 table without a contents variable, or an instance that does not serve json-stat2, gives zero rows or NULL; a field the source does not state is NA.

Examples

# \donttest{
scb <- px_api("scb", lang = "en")
if (px_available(scb)) {
  get_contents(scb, "TAB638")
}# }
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   table_id variable     code     text   unit  decimals measuring_type price_type
#>   <chr>    <chr>        <chr>    <chr>  <chr>    <int> <chr>          <chr>     
#> 1 TAB638   ContentsCode BE0101N1 Popul… numb…        0 Stock          NotApplic…
#> 2 TAB638   ContentsCode BE0101N2 Popul… numb…        0 Flow           NotApplic…
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: adjustment <chr>, refperiod <chr>, base_period <chr>
